claims.text: Agent/skill count is not a quality metric; runtime fan-out should scale with unresolved information and consequence.
Multi-agent debate should be selected dynamically and compared against a strong single-pass/deterministic baseline.
Skills should encode reusable capability/procedure while workflow runtime owns orchestration, execution, state and recovery.
OpenAI Codex current capability packaging is plugin-first; the former standalone openai/skills repository is deprecated for current deployment guidance.
Anthropic skills use self-contained SKILL.md packages, but target-environment behavior must be separately tested.
Google ADK 2.0 is a breaking-change boundary for agent API, event model and session schema.
Repository artifacts, deterministic tests, hosted CI, provider-live runtime execution and final deployment are distinct truth states.
The current three-layer convergence is archive/vault (PR #46), portable reasoning/skills (PR #45), and durable execution/control-plane (PR #29).

obligations.text: Every final completion claim maps each user acceptance criterion to direct evidence.
Every cross-platform adapter records host/runtime family, version/date, OS, permissions, and target-runtime verification status.
Every multi-agent execution records chosen topology, active roles/actors, branch ownership, stop reason, and verifier outcome.
Unknown, unsupported, unavailable, blocked and impossible remain distinct states.
Failure classification precedes retry; a retry must change method, evidence, tool/model, representation, assumption or environment.
A skill/configuration is not called compatible until the target runtime/version is tested or explicitly marked unverified.
CI-blocked PR #45 remains Draft until hosted jobs actually start and pass or the blocker is explicitly accepted.
